properties.decision:
RECORDED AS A FINDING PLUS AN OPEN QUESTION, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised 2026-08-04 while answering Anthony's dev_storyflow question (req:no-idea-goes-quiet). Nothing here is settled.

THE FINDING, VERIFIED IN CODE RATHER THAN SUPPOSED. `unsatisfied_requirement` fires per Requirement with no incoming SATISFIES, and it is NOT an aggregate gap — checked in `GapSource::is_aggregate()` (crates/reflow2-core/src/detect.rs), where `UnvalidatedCapability` is the sole `true` arm and `UnsatisfiedRequirement` is listed exhaustively among the `false` ones, with the comment that per-node keying is deliberate so a change to the named set expires the judgement. CONSEQUENCE: ingesting a corpus of 300 ideas that nothing yet implements produces 300 gaps that all say the same thing, burying every distinct finding beneath them.

THIS IS [BL-145] AT AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE. That row reads: "One detector produced 27 of 49 gaps saying the same thing, and buried every distinct finding below the fold" — found 2026-08-01 by an /adopt pass over music_graph. It was filed at 27 against 49. A captured corpus is where it stops being a presentation annoyance: at 300 it is not noise, it is a wall, and it lands on exactly the user whose whole reason for ingesting was to stop losing track of things.

⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY BL-145 RESTATED, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Every existing detector was designed against a design that is MOSTLY BUILT, where an unsatisfied requirement is an exception worth naming one at a time. A captured corpus inverts the base rate: unbuilt is the NORMAL state, unbuilt is CORRECT, and req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design already says so explicitly — "every capability is `planned`, every requirement `proposed`, and the as-built half of the loop has no subject — which is honest and must not read as catastrophic." So the defect is not that the detector is chatty. It is that the detector's severity model encodes an assumption about the design's phase that the corpus case falsifies. The same suspicion should be carried to `unrealized_capability`, `unallocated_capability`, `design_without_build` and `build_without_verification`, none of which were checked here.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) MAKE IT AGGREGATE when the count crosses a bar — one gap saying "300 requirements are unsatisfied", drilling down on request. Cheapest, and `is_aggregate` is the existing seam. Counter, and the code comment states it directly: aggregate keying means a standing judgement does not expire when the set changes, so a requirement added later is silently covered by a judgement made before it existed — which is the right trade for a rollup and the wrong one for a finding that names nodes. (b) BAND BY PHASE — read the project's mode or the design's position on the maturity trajectory, and let a design with nothing built report this as a reading rather than as gaps. Fits maturity_report's existing frontier computation and dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written. Counter: it makes gap severity depend on a computed phase, and reflow2 has been careful that "where this design SHOULD be is deliberately not stated". (c) SCOPE IT — detect_gaps already takes a `scope` seed, so the corpus user asks per region rather than globally. Counter: it requires the user to already know which region to ask about, which is precisely what someone who just ingested 1,124 documents does not know. (d) DO NOTHING TO THE DETECTOR AND FIX THE PRESENTATION — group identical gap_sources in the report and lead with the distinct ones. Counter: `detect_gaps` is consumed by agents and by CI, not only by the report, so a presentation-only fix leaves both other consumers buried.

WHAT THIS REPRIORITISES, offered as an observation and not as a plan. `epoch:v0240-planned` sequences the corpus increment as ingest-then-know-where-you-stopped. This finding says a fifth thing sits between them: a corpus that ingests correctly and then buries its own findings has not delivered req:no-idea-goes-quiet, whose whole content is that an unbuilt idea must stay LOUD. Loud and unreadable are not the same state, and 300 identical gaps is the second one. Whether that makes it a v0.24.0 obligation or a v0.25.0 one is Anthony's call — [BL-205] and [BL-194], both already scheduled for v0.25.0 as "the loop tells the truth about what it is owed", are the same family and may want to travel together.

NOT VERIFIED HERE, and it bears on which option is right: whether `acknowledge_gaps` (the bulk form) already makes 300 gaps tractable by letting one reason dispose of many at once. If it does, the wall is lower than stated and (d) rises. Nobody checked.
properties.name: OPEN — how should gap reporting behave when most requirements are legitimately unbuilt, as a captured corpus makes normal?
properties.rationale: Recorded now rather than as a backlog row because it is a defect against a shipped capability with a real fork behind it, and this session has just spent an hour establishing that the backlog is where such things go to be re-derived. The measurement (is_aggregate checked in source, BL-145's 27-of-49 as the prior instance) is written down so the next session argues from the code rather than from the impression that gap output is noisy. Kept separate from req:no-idea-goes-quiet because that node states what the user needs and this one asks how the machine should behave — one node holding both could only ever be half-answered. The unchecked item (bulk acknowledge) is named explicitly so its absence is visible as a hole rather than passing as a completed analysis.
